newsitem.title: CHINA: Airbus, Alenia, China, S'pore to make 100-seat jet.
newsitem.headline: Airbus, Alenia, China, S'pore to make 100-seat jet.

text.p: Airbus Industrie, Finmeccanica of Italy's Alenia, Aviation Industries of China AVIC and Singapore Technologies Aerospace signed an agreement in Beijing on Thursday to manufacture a 100-seat jet airliner.
The agreement brings Italy's Alenia into the consortium to produce the 100-seat regional airliner that will be assembled in China.

Officials were unable to give a new breakdown for equity in the venture, but sources close to the deal said Airbus and Alenia together would hold about a 39 percent stake. Of that, Alenia would hold about 38 percent, they said.

In June 1996, AVIC, a European consortium and Singapore Technologies Aerospace signed a contract to develop the 100-seater with the Chinese side taking 46 percent and the Singapore partner holding 15 percent of the project, valued at about $2.0 billion.
The project is expected to build about 1,000 jets mainly for Asian regional carriers.
The contract signed on Thursday was a framework agreement, with the new family of jets set to enter service by the year 2003, Airbus said in a statement.
The new aircraft family would initially produce two versions of 105 seats and 125 seats and would benefit from commonality with Airbus to capture a significant share of the world market, Airbus said.

The venture would be managed by a joint venture set up in China, with the European partners bringing expertise and technology in engineering, production, quality control and product support services, Airbus said.
